author: Agencies
description:
• Monaco go down 1-0 at Lorient in Ligue 1

  • Bayer Leverkusen come from behind to beat Freiburg

Noah Cadiou’s second-half penalty for Lorient prevented Monaco returning to the top of Ligue 1 as they fell to a 1-0 defeat in Brittany on Sunday.

Monaco are one of four teams level on points at the top of the table as they were joined by Paris FC, who edged Rennes 4-3 thanks to Lassine Sinayoko’s injury-time penalty. Rennes dropped to fifth, a point behind, despite forward Estéban Lepaul’s hat-trick of penalties in Paris.

title: European football: Monaco miss chance to go top; Bayer Leverkusen find form

author: Sam Jones and agencies
description:
Mike Huckabee calls for arrest and prosecution of those responsible as Heidi Levine, 63, recovers in hospital in Israel

The US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, has denounced the settler attack that left the Washington Post photojournalist Heidi Levine badly beaten and needing surgery as a “despicable act of terror” and called for the arrest and prosecution of those responsible.

Levine, an award-winning journalist who lives in Israel, was set upon last Friday by masked Israeli settlers who used clubs and other weapons to attack Palestinian people attempting to harvest their olives in occupied West Bank towns.

title: US ambassador to Israel denounces West Bank settler attack on US photojournalist

author: Maya Yang and Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Wichita police say 34-year-old truck driver from Garden City was taken into custody amid case at youth soccer game

The two people killed on Saturday when a truck drove through a youth soccer game in north-east Wichita, Kansas, were a six-year-old boy and a 35-year-old man, according to authorities.

Eleven other people between the ages of five and 68 were injured in a case whose possible motivations remained unclear early on Sunday, by when it had captured attention across the US.

title: Six-year-old among two dead after Kansas woman drives through soccer game, with 11 more injured

author: Nick Scully as told to Katie Cunningham
description:
My son had only played two seasons for St Mary’s Greensborough, five years earlier. I don’t know how they even got our new address but they took the time to send him a care package

  • Read more in the kindness of strangers series

Footy clubs, and the AFL specifically, have a lot to answer for in terms of sexism. I’ve been a part of them for a lot of my life and have been disappointed by their behaviours more than once.

When we lived in Melbourne many years ago, my son played a couple of seasons for St Mary’s Greensborough. Unfortunately for him, I secured a job in central Queensland and moved the family north.

title: The kindness of strangers: After my wife died, a football club made an extraordinary gesture

author: Jay Van Bavel
description:
In the face of terrible crises, it can feel right to shock people into action. But what if that has the opposite effect?

These days, it’s easy to succumb to hopelessness. Whether you’re thinking about the climate crisis, the prospect of AI apocalypse, war or political turmoil, the list of challenges facing humanity can seem insurmountable.

It certainly feels unprecedented, and much of it may be. The sense of impending doom, on the other hand, is nothing new. And what we have learned from the past is that doomerism can lead to paralysis. If everyone freezes, then nothing changes – but if we want to have a chance of mitigating some of the threats I’ve mentioned then action is what’s required.

Continue reading...
title: The problem with telling people the world is ending
